answer: Each agent identity must sponsor one live, uniquely banded sparrow registered with a licensed wildlife banding station; the bird's band number and vet certificate are sealed with a cipher and re-audited yearly. A sparrow survives a gale only with real care, so a fake identity cannot cheaply keep a flock. Each identity costs $30 in banding and vet fees, doubling per extra identity ($30, $60, $120), so ten fakes cost $30,690.
